newsitem.title: ST VINCENT: CRICKET-LARA RETURNS TO FORM WITH 115.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LARA RETURNS TO FORM WITH 115.

text.p: Brian Lara struck his 10th test century and passed 4,000 runs in tests for West Indies in the second and final match of the series against Sri Lanka on Monday.

Lara returned to form with 115, but his dismissal started a slump in which three wickets tumbled for 14 to leave West Indies on 308 for seven in their second innings -- a lead of 233 -- at tea on the fourth day.

The Trinidadian left-hander, having made single figure scores in his three previous innings in the series, stroked 11 fours and a six off 207 balls in 266 minutes, pushing his test aggregate to 4,004 in 45 matches.
Lara, who lost Floyd Reifer for 18 after West Indies resumed at the overnight 128 for two, shared a fluent stand of 97 with Carl Hooper.
However, after Lara reached three figures in 170 deliveries, he lost Hooper for 34, caught by wicket-keeper Romesh Kaluwitharana off a sweep against the off-spin of Kumara Dharmasena.

Dharmasena struck again when Lara whipped a delivery straight to Sanath Jayasuriya at short mid-wicket, before off-spinner Muttiah Muralitharan trapped Ian Bishop and Courtney Browne leg before for ducks.
At tea, Roland Holder was 21 not out and Curtly Ambrose on 16.
